claims.text: Additive manufacturing with controlled cooling can create a nanograined surface layer and a coarse-grained core in an HEA.
The resulting gradient microstructure synergistically improves strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance relative to homogeneous processing.
Precisely controlled thermal gradients during solidification can deliberately induce the proposed microstructural gradient.
Minimal post-processing will preserve the engineered microstructural gradient.
A well-managed printing thermal field can establish a gradual transition between a hard nanograined region and a tougher coarse-grained region.
Excessively rapid or uneven cooling can produce porosity or undesirable residual stresses.
Porosity or excessive residual stresses can negate the mechanical benefits of the gradient structure.
The method is limited to alloy compositions whose solidification behavior permits stable gradient formation.
A nanograined surface increases strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
A nanograined surface increases stiffness through grain-boundary strengthening.
A coarse-grained core preserves ductility.
A coarse-grained core preserves fracture resistance.
Controlled segregation or nanoscale precipitates at the gradient interface can further balance the mechanical response.
Fine grains elevate yield strength.
Fine grains elevate elastic modulus.
The coarse-grained interior provides plasticity and dissipates energy during crack propagation.
The dual-region structure creates barriers to crack initiation while retaining toughness.
The gradient-structured alloy is expected to improve fracture toughness by approximately 10–20% relative to homogeneous HEAs.
The gradient-structured alloy is expected to improve ductility by approximately 10–20% relative to homogeneous HEAs.
The gradient-structured alloy is expected to maintain or slightly enhance tensile strength and Young’s modulus relative to homogeneous HEAs.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis asserts enhancement of all four properties, whereas the predicted outcome allows tensile strength and Young’s modulus merely to be maintained rather than improved.
